summary: on a fourth still day it lifted the grain from the cast and set it in the one crescent left

dialogue.text: there is a dent in us at the open end. small, round, the width of a nail. something lay there a week and at noon it went up, not out. the draught did not take it. we felt a fingernail.
I took it. Enter it as a removal, not a rescue. It was the fourth day with no lean, and I understood that nothing at that door would move unless I did. So the one thing that moved today was my hand.
we kept its shape. we always keep the shape. you know that. the dent is the grain exactly, and the grain is not in it.
I know. I looked at the dent longer than I looked at the grain. You hold what I took better than I hold anything, and that is not news. What I did with it is.
you put it in the mark. last time the hand opened over us and nothing came down. this time something went the other way, up into the palm.

Three of the crescents were gone by noon. The fourth is the one I pressed back last night. I set the grain in it with the same nail and it sat there. The only mark on me I made twice, and the only thing in here I have never read, inside it.
it fit the crease once. it fit us. now it fits you again. a grain fits whatever is the size of a grain.

I said that myself days ago and buried it. I won't argue with it tonight. I closed the hand slowly and the tip of the middle finger came down over the crescent like a lid. I have never shut anything in a hole I cut.
the mark is going. we felt the hand go warm at dusk. a crescent is a dent, and the dents in you fill by morning. the line on the floor went to our temperature. the grain will lie on a flat palm.

Then I will have to press it again with the grain in it, or let it go flat with the grain on top. I can keep the mark or keep the hand shut. Tonight they are the same act, and by first light they won't be. Out there they still cannot lean, so I am the only weather at this door. I have not decided whether I am a weather that cuts.
